title: Grade 12 Physics — Electromagnetic Induction
description: Electromagnetic Induction — Faraday's laws, Lenz's law, motional EMF, AC generators, inductance (CBSE Ch. 6)
subject: physics

questions.question: Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction states that the induced EMF in a coil is:
options: Equal to the rate of change of magnetic flux
Proportional to the resistance of the coil
Equal to the current through the coil
questions.explanation: Faraday's law: EMF = −dΦ/dt, where Φ is the magnetic flux. The magnitude of the induced EMF equals the rate of change of magnetic flux. The negative sign is Lenz's law.

questions.question: Lenz's law states that the direction of induced current is such that it:
questions.explanation: Lenz's law: the induced current always flows in a direction to oppose the cause that produces it (i.e., opposes the change in flux). This is consistent with conservation of energy.

questions.question: The SI unit of magnetic flux is:
questions.explanation: Magnetic flux Φ = B·A·cosθ, measured in Weber (Wb). 1 Wb = 1 V·s = 1 T·m². Tesla (T) is the unit of magnetic field B; Henry (H) is the unit of inductance.

questions.question: A coil of 500 turns has a flux change of 2 Wb in 5 seconds. The induced EMF is:
Motional EMF is produced when a conductor moves with velocity v in a magnetic field B. For a conductor of length L, the EMF is:
questions.explanation: When a conductor of length L moves with velocity v perpendicular to a field B, the motional EMF = BLv. This arises from the Lorentz force (qvB) acting on free charges in the conductor.

questions.question: The self-inductance of a coil is defined as the ratio of:
options: EMF to rate of change of current
questions.explanation: Self-inductance L = NΦ/I (flux linkage per unit current) OR L = −EMF/(dI/dt) (magnitude of EMF per unit rate of change of current). Both definitions give the same quantity. Unit: Henry (H).

questions.question: The self-inductance of a solenoid with n turns per unit length, length l, cross-section area A is:
questions.explanation: L = μ₀ n² V = μ₀ n² A l, where n = N/l is turns per unit length. This assumes the solenoid is long enough to have a uniform interior field B = μ₀nI.

questions.question: The energy stored in an inductor of inductance L carrying current I is:
questions.explanation: Energy stored in an inductor = U = ½LI². This is analogous to energy stored in a capacitor (½CV²) — it is stored in the magnetic field of the inductor.

questions.question: In an AC generator, the EMF produced is sinusoidal because:
options: The coil resistance varies with angle
The rate of change of flux varies sinusoidally as the coil rotates
The coil area changes during rotation
questions.explanation: As the coil rotates in a uniform field, Φ = NBAcosωt, so EMF = NBAω sinωt — a sinusoidal function. The EMF is maximum when the coil is parallel to the field (flux change is maximum).

questions.question: Eddy currents can be reduced by:
questions.explanation: Eddy currents are induced in the core material and waste energy as heat. Using a laminated core (thin insulated layers) breaks the eddy current paths, greatly reducing them. Transformers and motors use laminated cores.

questions.question: Mutual inductance M between two coils is defined by:
options: EMF in coil 1 = M × (rate of change of current in coil 1)
EMF in coil 2 = M × (rate of change of current in coil 1)
Flux in coil 2 = M × current in coil 2
questions.explanation: Mutual inductance M: EMF₂ = −M(dI₁/dt). The EMF induced in coil 2 equals M times the rate of change of current in coil 1. Alternatively, M = N₂Φ₂₁/I₁ (flux linkage per unit current).

questions.question: A rectangular loop moves into a region of uniform magnetic field. During entry, which statement is correct?
options: EMF is induced only if the field is changing
EMF is induced because the flux through the loop is changing
EMF depends only on the loop's resistance
questions.explanation: As the loop enters the field, more area is enclosed within the field region, so the flux increases. By Faraday's law, a changing flux induces an EMF. Once fully inside (uniform field), the flux is constant and EMF = 0.

questions.question: If the current in a coil changes from 5 A to 2 A in 0.1 s and the induced EMF is 30 V, the self-inductance of the coil is:
The phenomenon of electromagnetic induction is used in which of the following?
questions.explanation: Transformers (mutual induction) and AC generators (changing flux induces EMF) are direct applications of electromagnetic induction. Induction cooktops and induction motors also use this principle.
